cards.title: The Man Sleeping a Hundred Years Beside His Donkey and Unspoiled Food
cards.note: Surah 2:259 recounts a traveler questioning how a ruined city will be restored, sleeping for a hundred years beside his food and his donkey while supposing a single day has passed, matching the Talmudic narrative of Honi ha-Me'aggel in Taanit 23a.

discussion.view: Commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir identify the traveler variously as Ezra (`Uzayr`), Jeremiah, or Khidr passing by Jerusalem after its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar.
discussion.reply: In Talmud Bavli Taanit 23a, Honi ha-Me'aggel questions how the 70-year Babylonian exile of Jerusalem relates to Psalm 126:1, falls asleep beside his donkey and food for 70 years, and wakes to learn that generations have passed. Surah 2:259 fuses this Talmudic sleeper-and-donkey narrative with Ezekiel's vision of dry bones clothed with sinews and flesh in Ezekiel 37:7–8.

cards.quranEn: Or (have you not considered) the example of the one who passed by a town that had collapsed in ruins? He said, ‘How will God give this (town) life after its death?’ So God caused him to die for a hundred years, (and) then raised him up. He said, ‘How long have you remained (dead)?’ He said, ‘I have remained (dead) for a day or part of a day.’ He said, ‘No! You have remained (dead) for a hundred years. Look at your food and drink, it has not spoiled, and look at your donkey – and (this happened) so that We might make you a sign to the people – and look at the bones, how We raise them up, (and) then clothe them with flesh.’ So when it became clear to him, he said, ‘I know that God is powerful over everything.’
quranHighlights: So God caused him to die for a hundred years, (and) then raised him up.
Look at your food and drink, it has not spoiled, and look at your donkey

cards.title: Potiphar's Wife Threatening Joseph in Yoma 35b
cards.note: Surah 12:30–34 depicts Potiphar's wife demanding Joseph's submission and threatening him beforehand with imprisonment and humiliation unless he obeys her command, paralleling her explicit prison threat in Talmud Bavli Yoma 35b.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators present the banquet of the Egyptian women and the verbal threats of Potiphar's wife as revealed historical details expanding the brief account of Joseph's temptation.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 39:7–20, Potiphar's wife propositions Joseph in private and has him imprisoned after he flees, without first threatening him with prison to coerce his compliance. That explicit pre-imprisonment threat appears in fifth-century rabbinic literature in Talmud Bavli Yoma 35b, where she tells Joseph she will incarcerate him in prison and bend his stature with suffering if he refuses to submit.

cards.quranEn: [30] Some women in the city said, ‘The wife of that mighty one has been trying to seduce her young man. He has affected her deeply (with) love. Surely we see (that) she is indeed clearly astray.’ [31] When she heard their cunning (gossip), she sent for them, and prepared a banquet for them, and gave each one of them a knife. Then she said (to Joseph), ‘Come forth to (wait on) them.’ When they saw him, they admired him, and cut their hands, and said, ‘God preserve (us)! This is no (mere) mortal. This is nothing but a splendid angel!’ [32] She said, ‘That is the one you blamed me about. I certainly did try to seduce him, but he defended himself, and (now) if he does not do what I command him, he will indeed be imprisoned, and become one of the disgraced.’ [33] He said, ‘My Lord, prison is preferable to me than what they invite me to. But unless You turn their plot away from me, I shall give in to them, and I shall become one of the ignorant.’ [34] Then his Lord responded to him, and turned their plot away from him. Surely He – He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
quranHighlights: I certainly did try to seduce him, but he defended himself, and (now) if he does not do what I command him, he will indeed be imprisoned, and become one of the disgraced

cards.title: Noah Remaining Among His People Nine Hundred and Fifty Years Before the Flood
cards.note: Surah 29:14–15 states that Noah stayed among his people 'a thousand years minus fifty years' (950 years) before the Flood, assigning Noah's 950-year total lifespan from Genesis 9:29 to his pre-Flood mission instead of the 600 years of Genesis 7:6.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as Ibn Abbas (in al-Tabari) and Ibn Kathir explain that Noah preached to his people for 950 years before the Flood and lived additional centuries afterward.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 7:6 and 9:28–29, Noah is 600 years old when the Flood begins, lives 350 years after the Flood, and dies at a total age of 950 years. Surah 29:14 retains the exact biblical number 950 ('a thousand years minus fifty years') while placing the entire 950-year span prior to the Flood.

cards.quranEn: [14] Certainly We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years, minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them while they were doing evil. [15] But We rescued him and (his) companions on the ship, and made it a miracle for all peoples.
quranHighlights: We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years, minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them

cards.title: Demons in Solomon's Reign and the Two Angels Harut and Marut in Babylon
cards.note: Surah 2:102 links demons in Solomon's kingdom teaching magic with two angels in Babylon named Harut and Marut, combining 1 Enoch 7–8 on fallen angels teaching sorcery with Talmud Gittin 68a on Solomon's male and female demons.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes explain that Surah 2:102 exonerates Solomon of practicing sorcery while affirming that God sent two angels, Harut and Marut, to Babylon as a test regarding magic.
discussion.reply: The narrative combines three Near Eastern traditions: Talmudic legends in Gittin 68a giving Solomon authority over demons, the Second Temple Book of Watchers (1 Enoch 7–8) where angels descend and teach humans charms and root-cuttings, and the paired Zoroastrian archangels (`Amesha Spentas`) Haurvatat/Horvadad and Ameretat/Amerodad, whose Middle Persian names correspond philologically to Harut and Marut.

cards.quranEn: And they followed what the satans used to recite over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the satans disbelieved. They taught the people magic, and what had been sent down to the two angels (in) Babylon, Hārūt and Mārūt. Neither of them taught anyone, unless they both (first) said, ‘We are only a temptation, so do not disbelieve.’ And they learned from both of them how to separate a husband from his wife. Yet they did not harm anyone in this way, except by the permission of God. What they learned (only) harmed them and did not benefit them. Certainly they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter. Evil indeed is what they have sold themselves for, if (only) they knew.

cards.title: Transgressors Transformed into Apes as Divine Punishment in Sanhedrin 109a
cards.note: Surah 2:65–66 recounts God punishing Israelite Sabbath violators by commanding them, 'Become apes, skulking away,' paralleling the Talmudic punishment in Sanhedrin 109a where rebels against God are transformed into apes.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir state that an Israelite coastal community violated the Sabbath by trapping fish on Saturday and was physically transformed into apes for three days before perishing.
discussion.reply: In the Torah (Exodus 31:14–15; Numbers 15:32–36), the penalty for Sabbath violation is capital execution, and no biblical passage records humans being transformed into apes. Physical transformation of rebels against God into apes (`kofim`) is a rabbinic aggadic punishment recorded by Rabbi Yirmeya bar Elazar in Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 109a.

quranHighlights: those of you who transgressed in (the matter of) the sabbath, and (that) We said to them, ‘Become apes, skulking away!’

cards.title: Four Sequential Embryological Stages Clothed With Bones and Flesh
cards.note: Surah 23:12–14 describes human development from clay extract to a drop of fluid (`nutfah`), a clot (`alaqah`), a lump (`mudghah`), and bones clothed with flesh, matching the blood-and-flesh gestational stages in Talmud Bavli Niddah 25a.

discussion.view: Traditional and modern commentators present the four stages in Surah 23:12–14—drop, clot, lump, and bones clothed with flesh—as revealed scientific knowledge of human gestation.
discussion.reply: Each stage mirrors Late Antique medical and rabbinic models: Talmud Bavli Niddah 25a distinguishes early gestational sacs 'full of blood' from the subsequent stage 'full of flesh' (cf. Niddah 30b–31a), while Galen's De Semine (On Semen I.8–10, CMG V 3,1) divides embryogenesis into four sequential stages from seminal fluid to a blood-filled coagulum, an unarticulated fleshy mass, and hardened bones subsequently clothed with muscle.

cards.quranEn: [12] Certainly We created the human from an extract of clay. [13] Then We made him a drop in a secure dwelling place, [14] then We made a clot (from) the drop, then We made a lump (from) the clot, then We made bones (from) the lump, then We clothed the bones (with) flesh, (and) then We (re)produced him as another creature. So blessed (be) God, the best of creators!

cards.title: Pharaoh Boasting to Moses: Do Not These Rivers of Egypt Flow Beneath Me
cards.note: Surah 43:46–56 places into the mouth of the Exodus Pharaoh confronting Moses the boast 'Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers which flow beneath me,' attributing to him Pharaoh Hophra's Nile boast in Ezekiel 29:2–3.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that Rameses or the Pharaoh of the Exodus boasted before his assembly of Egypt's Nile canals and tributaries to belittle Moses prior to the drowning in the Red Sea.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, the Pharaoh of the Exodus confronts Moses by the Nile (Exodus 5:2; 7:15), whereas the specific boast 'The rivers are mine, and I made them' belongs to Pharaoh Hophra (Apries, r. 589–570 BC) in Ezekiel 29:2–3 and 29:9, more than six centuries after the Exodus.

cards.quranEn: [46] Certainly We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his assembly. He said, ‘Surely I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.’ [47] But when he brought them Our signs, suddenly they began to laugh at them, [48] even though every sign We showed them was greater than the one before it. We seized them with the punishment, so that they might return. [49] They said, ‘Magician! Call on your Lord for us by whatever covenant He has made with you, (and) surely we shall indeed be (rightly) guided.’ [50] But when We removed the punishment from them, immediately they broke (their promise). [51] Pharaoh called out among his people: ‘My people! Is the kingdom of Egypt not mine, and these rivers (which) flow beneath me? Do you not see? [52] Am I not better than this (man), who is despicable and scarcely makes (things) clear? [53] If only bracelets of gold were cast (down) on him or the accompanying angels came with him.’ [54] So he unsettled his people, and they obeyed him. Surely they were a wicked people. [55] When they had angered Us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them – all (of them)! [56] We made them a thing of the past, and an example for the later (generations).

cards.title: Earth Created Before the Heavens and Seven Heavens Formed from Smoke
cards.note: Surah 41:9–12 places the earth's creation and mountains before the fashioning of seven heavens from smoke, matching Beit Hillel's earth-first order in Talmud Chagigah 12a and the seven firmaments of Chagigah 12b.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir harmonize the sequence in 41:9–12 with 79:27–30 by distinguishing the initial creation of the unformed earth before the seven heavens from the later spreading out (daha) of the terrestrial surface after the sky was completed.
discussion.reply: Genesis 1:1–8 places the firmament of heaven on the second day before dry land and plants appear on the third day. In Talmud Bavli Chagigah 12a–12b, Beit Hillel argues that the earth was created before the heavens, and Reish Lakish enumerates seven distinct firmaments by name, providing the rabbinic cosmology echoed in 41:9–12.

cards.quranEn: [9] Say: ‘Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and do you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. [10] He placed on it firm mountains (towering) above it, and blessed it, and decreed for it its (various) foods in four days, equal to the ones who ask. [11] Then He mounted (upward) to the sky, while it was (still) smoke, and said to it and to the earth, “Come, both of you, willingly or unwillingly!” They both said, “We come willingly.” [12] He finished them (as) seven heavens in two days, and inspired each heaven (with) its affair. And We adorned the sky of this world with lamps, and (made them) a protection. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing.’

sources.workSub: Talmud Bavli Chagigah 12a (Rabbinic Debate on the Order of Creation of Heaven and Earth)
sources.en: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute the order of Creation, as the Sages taught: Beit Shammai say: The heavens were created first and afterward the earth was created, as it is stated: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth” (Genesis 1:1), which indicates that heaven came first. And Beit Hillel say: The earth was created first, and heaven after it, as it is stated: “On the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven” (Genesis 2:4).

cards.title: Two Gardens of Sheba Swept Away by the Flood of the Marib Dam
cards.note: Surah 34:15–19 recounts how Sheba's two irrigated gardens on the right and left were swept away by the Flood of the Dam (Sayl al-'Arim), corresponding to the South Arabian Marib Dam breaches celebrated in pre-Islamic poetry preserved in al-Tabari.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite South Arabian genealogists and pre-Islamic poets such as al-A'sha to identify al-'Arim as the great stone dam of Ma'rib built by Himyar and Saba', whose breach scattered the Sabaean tribes across Arabia.
discussion.reply: Epigraphic South Arabian inscriptions at Ma'rib (such as CIH 540 and CIH 541 from the fifth and sixth centuries AD) and pre-Islamic verses by al-A'sha document repeated breaches of the Ma'rib irrigation dam that turned its flanking oases into desert scrub, situating 34:15–19 in local Arabian historical memory.

cards.quranEn: [15] Certainly for Sheba there was a sign in their dwelling place – two gardens, on the right and left: ‘Eat from the provision of your Lord, and be thankful to Him. A good land and a forgiving Lord.’ [16] But they turned away, so We sent on them the flood of ‘Arim, and We replaced for them their two gardens (with) two gardens producing bitter fruit, and tamarisks, and a few lote trees. [17] We repaid them that because they disbelieved. We do not repay (anyone) but the ungrateful? [18] We set between them and the towns which We have blessed (other) towns (which are still) visible, and We measured out the traveling (distance) between them: ‘Travel among them by night and day in security!’ [19] But they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen (the distance) between our journeys.’ They did themselves evil, so We made them legendary, and We tore them completely to pieces. Surely in that are signs indeed for every patient (and) thankful one.

cards.title: The Wives of Noah and Lot Betraying Their Righteous Husbands
cards.note: Surah 66:10 presents the wives of Noah and Lot as disbelievers who betrayed their righteous husbands, matching Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 where Lot's wife betrays the angelic guests to the Sodomites by asking neighbors for salt.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that the betrayal in 66:10 was in religion rather than marital chastity: Noah's wife called her husband mad and informed on believers, while Lot's wife signaled the presence of handsome guests to the people of Sodom.
discussion.reply: Genesis 19:26 states that Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt without mentioning any plot against the guests. Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 supplies the narrative of betrayal, recording that she went to her neighbors asking for salt so the townsmen of Sodom would learn that guests were staying in Lot's house.

cards.quranEn: God has struck a parable for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them. Neither of them was of any use at all to either of them against God, when it was said, ‘Enter the Fire, both of you, with the ones who enter!’
quranHighlights: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot
They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them.

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 51:5 (Lot's Wife Betraying the Guests by Asking Neighbors for Salt)
sources.en: “His wife looked behind him, [and she became a pillar of salt]” – Rabbi Yitzḥak said: This was because she sinned with salt on that night that the angels came to Lot. What did she do? She went to all her neighbors and said to them: ‘Give me salt, as we have guests,’ and her intention was that the residents of the city should become aware of them. That is why “she became a pillar of salt.”

cards.title: Noah Rebuking His Generation and Mocked by the Chiefs Before the Flood
cards.note: Surah 11:25–35 expands the Flood narrative into a public debate where Noah warns his people and the chiefs mock him and challenge him to bring the punishment, matching Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 108b on Noah's rejected warnings.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir view the extended dialogue between Noah and the chiefs of his people in 11:25–35 as a prophetic history revealed to comfort Muhammad against similar rejection by the Quraysh leadership in Mecca.
discussion.reply: In Genesis 6–7, Noah receives God's command and builds the ark in silence without addressing a single word of rebuke to his contemporaries. Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin 108b supplies the preaching and mockery scene, portraying Noah rebuking his generation with words harsh as torches while they deride him and challenge his warning of a flood.

cards.quranEn: [25] Certainly We sent Noah to his people: ‘I am a clear warner for you. [26] Do not serve (anyone) but God! Surely I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.’ [27] The assembly of those who disbelieved of his people said, ‘We do not see you as (anything) but a human being like us, and we do not see following you (any) but the worst (and) most gullible of us. We do not see in you any superiority over us. No! We think you are liars.’ [28] He said, ‘My people! Do you see? If I (stand) on a clear sign from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been obscured for you, shall we compel you (to accept) it when you are unwilling? [29] My people! I do not ask you for any money for it. My reward (depends) only on God. I am not going to drive away those who believe. Surely they are going to meet their Lord, but I see that you are an ignorant people. [30] My people! Who would help me against God if I drove them away? Will you not take heed? [31] I do not say to you, “I possess the storehouses of God,” nor do I know the unseen. And I do not say, “I am an angel,” nor do I say to those your eyes look down on, “God will not give them any good.” God knows what is in them. Surely then I would indeed be one of the evildoers.’ [32] They said, ‘Noah! You have disputed with us, and disputed (too) much with us. Bring us what you promise us, if you are one of the truthful.’ [33] He said, ‘Only God will bring it to you, if He (so) pleases, and you will not escape. [34] My advice will not benefit you – (even) if I wish to advise you – if God wishes to make you err. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.’ [35] Or do they say, ‘He has forged it’? Say: ‘If I have forged it, my sin is on me, but I am free of the sins you commit.’

cards.title: First Human from Clay, Progeny from Fluid, and Threefold Endowment
cards.note: Surah 32:7–9 distinguishes creating the first human from clay, his progeny from 'despicable water' (ma' mahin), and God breathing His spirit to grant hearing, sight, and hearts, matching Pirkei Avot 3:1 ('putrid drop') and Talmud Niddah 31a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 32:7–9 separates Adam's original formation from clay from the reproduction of his descendants through seminal fluid, followed by the ensoulment of the fetus and the gift of sensory faculties.
discussion.reply: Genesis 2:7 describes Adam's formation from dust and the breath of life, while Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:1 coins the moral maxim that every human comes from a 'putrid drop' (tippah seruchah), rendered in Arabic as ma' mahin. Talmud Bavli Niddah 31a further assigns spirit, sight of the eye, hearing of the ear, and understanding of the heart specifically to God's contribution.

sources.title: Talmud Bavli, Tractate Niddah
sources.en: The Sages taught: There are three partners in the creation of a person: The Holy One, Blessed be He, and his father, and his mother. His father emits the white seed, from which the following body parts are formed: The bones, the sinews, the nails, the brain that is in its head, and the white of the eye. His mother emits red seed, from which are formed the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul, his countenance [ukelaster], eyesight, hearing of the ear, the capability of speech of the mouth, the capability of walking with the legs, understanding, and wisdom.

cards.title: Parable of the Boastful Vineyard Owner Whose Lush Estate Is Ruined
cards.note: Surah 18:32–44 portrays a rich man boasting over two hedged grape gardens before his harvest is ruined overnight, combining Jesus' Parable of the Rich Fool in Luke 12:16–21 with the hedged vineyard laid waste in Isaiah 5:1–6.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report from early exegetes that the parable of the two garden owners in 18:32–44 illustrates a believer and a disbeliever among the ancients (often identified as two brothers among the Israelites) to warn Mecca's wealthy elite.
discussion.reply: The Quranic parable merges two canonical biblical passages: Isaiah 5:1–6, where a fertile vineyard hedged and planted with choice vines is laid waste when rain is withheld, and Luke 12:16–21, where a rich landowner boasts to his soul over his stored harvest on the very night his life and estate are stripped away.

cards.quranEn: [32] Strike for them a parable of two men: We made for one of them two gardens of grapes, and surrounded both with date palms, and placed between them (a field of) crops. [33] Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail in any way. And We caused a river to gush forth between them. [34] And he had fruit. So he said to his companion, while he was talking with him, ‘I am greater than you in wealth, and mightier in family.’ [35] And he entered his garden, doing himself evil, (for) he said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish, [36] nor do I think the Hour is coming. If indeed I am returned to my Lord, I shall indeed find a better (place of) return than this.’ [37] His companion said to him, while he was talking with him, ‘Do you disbelieve in Him who created you from dust, then from a drop, (and) then fashioned you as a man? [38] But as for us, He is God, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. [39] Why did you not say, when you entered your garden, “What God pleases,” (for there is) no power except in God? If you see me as inferior to you in wealth and children, [40] it may be that my Lord will give me (something) better than your garden, and send on it a reckoning from the sky, so that it becomes slippery soil, [41] or its water sinks (into the earth), so that you will not be able to find it.’ [42] And (all) his fruit was overwhelmed, and in the morning he began wringing his hands over what he had spent on it, (for) it had collapsed on its trellises, and he said, ‘I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord!’ [43] But there was no cohort to help him, other than God, and he was helpless. [44] In such a case protection (belongs only) to God, the True One. He is best in reward, and best in final outcome.

cards.quranAr: ۞وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلٗا رَّجُلَيۡنِ جَعَلۡنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيۡنِ مِنۡ أَعۡنَٰبٖ وَحَفَفۡنَٰهُمَا بِنَخۡلٖ وَجَعَلۡنَا بَيۡنَهُمَا زَرۡعٗا ﴿32﴾ كِلۡتَا ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ ءَاتَتۡ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمۡ تَظۡلِم مِّنۡهُ شَيۡـٔٗاۚ وَفَجَّرۡنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرٗا ﴿33﴾ وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرٞ فَقَالَ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكۡثَرُ مِنكَ مَالٗا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرٗا ﴿34﴾ وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٞ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدٗا ﴿35﴾ وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةٗ وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيۡرٗا مِّنۡهَا مُنقَلَبٗا ﴿36﴾ قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرۡتَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٖ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطۡفَةٖ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلٗا ﴿37﴾ لَّـٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدٗا ﴿38﴾ وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالٗا وَوَلَدٗا ﴿39﴾ فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّيٓ أَن يُؤۡتِيَنِ خَيۡرٗا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡهَا حُسۡبَانٗا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصۡبِحَ صَعِيدٗا زَلَقًا ﴿40﴾ أَوۡ يُصۡبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوۡرٗا فَلَن تَسۡتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبٗا ﴿41﴾ وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصۡبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيۡهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُشۡرِكۡ بِرَبِّيٓ أَحَدٗا ﴿42﴾ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ فِئَةٞ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا ﴿43﴾ هُنَالِكَ ٱلۡوَلَٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ هُوَ خَيۡرٞ ثَوَابٗا وَخَيۡرٌ عُقۡبٗا ﴿44﴾

cards.title: Priests Casting Their Pens as Lots to Decide Who Will Guard Mary
cards.note: Surah 3:42–44 cites as unseen knowledge how the temple priests disputed and cast their pens or rods (aqlamahum) as lots to determine who would become Mary's guardian, matching the lot-casting in the Protevangelium of James 8:2–9:1.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that the temple priests cast their reed pens into the Jordan River to settle their dispute over who would raise the child Mary after Zechariah claimed priority through his marriage to her maternal aunt.
discussion.reply: The canonical Gospels never place Mary's upbringing inside the Jerusalem Temple or mention a priestly lottery for her guardianship. That episode comes from the second-century Greek Protevangelium of James 8:2–9:1, where the high priest Zacharias summons the widowers to bring their rods to the Temple so a sign may designate who will take the virgin of the Lord into his keeping.

cards.quranEn: [42] And (remember) when the angels said, ‘Mary! Surely God has chosen you and purified you, and He has chosen you over all other women. [43] Mary! Be obedient to your Lord, and prostrate yourself and bow with the ones who bow.’ [44] – That is one of the stories of the unseen. We inspired you (with) it. You were not with them when they cast their pens (as lots to see) which of them would take charge of Mary. Nor were you with them when they were disputing. –

cards.title: Surah 5 Review of Jesus' Clay Birds, Healings, and Sorcery Accusation
cards.note: In God's direct address to Jesus in 5:110, breathing life into a clay bird stands alongside speaking in the cradle and the Israelites calling his signs 'clear magic,' matching the Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 and Talmud Sanhedrin 43a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir read 5:110 as God's covenantal reminder to Jesus enumerating the miracles granted to him by divine permission (bi-idhni) to distinguish prophetic signs from divine sonship.
discussion.reply: Unlike 3:49, where Jesus announces these signs to Israel, 5:110 frames them as God's retrospective address and adds the Israelites' charge that his signs were 'clear magic.' That passage unites the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 (animating clay sparrows) with the rabbinic verdict in Talmud Sanhedrin 43a that Jesus practiced sorcery and led Israel astray.

cards.quranEn: (Remember) when God said, ‘Jesus, son of Mary! Remember My blessing on you and on your mother, when I supported you with the holy spirit, (and) you spoke to the people (while you were still) in the cradle, and in adulthood. And when I taught you the Book and the wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel. And when you created the form of a bird from clay by My permission, and you breathed into it, and it became a bird by My permission, and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission. And when you brought forth the dead by My permission, and when I restrained the Sons of Israel from (violence against) you. When you brought them the clear signs, those among them who had disbelieved said, “This is nothing but clear magic.”’

cards.title: God Commanding the Furnace to Be Coolness and Peace for Abraham
cards.note: In Surah 21:68–70, the crowd cries 'Burn him and help your gods' and God commands the fire to be 'coolness and peace for Abraham,' following the midrashic reading of 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Genesis 11:28) as a fiery furnace in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir narrate from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that Nimrod and his people built an enclosure of firewood, hurled Abraham into the blaze by catapult, and saw the flames rendered harmless by God's decree 'O fire, be coolness and peace.'
discussion.reply: In Genesis 11:28, 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Hebrew Ur Kasdim, rendered in the Greek Septuagint as 'the country of the Chaldees') is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham's birth. Because the Hebrew noun ur also means 'fire' or 'flame,' Jewish exegetes in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13 read Ur Kasdim as 'the fiery furnace of the Chaldeans,' generating the narrative of Nimrod casting Abraham into the furnace echoed in 21:68–70.

sources.en: He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod. He [Nimrod] said to him [Abraham]: ‘Let us bow down to fire.’ Abraham said to him: ‘Let us better bow down to water, that extinguishes fire.’ Nimrod said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to water.’ He said to him: ‘If so, let us bow down to the clouds, that bear the water.’ He said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to the clouds.’ He said to him: ‘If so, let us bow down to the wind, that scatters the clouds.’ He said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to the wind.’ He said to him: ‘Better let us bow down to a person, who can withstand the wind.’ He said to him: ‘You are saying mere words. cards.title: Dhu l-Qarnayn Reaching the Muddy Spring of the Setting Sun and the East
cards.note: Surah 18:83–91 narrates Dhu l-Qarnayn ('The Two-Horned One') traveling to the sun's setting place in a muddy spring and to its rising place over a shelterless people, matching the journeys of Alexander the Great in the Syriac Christian Legend.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record early reports identifying Dhu l-Qarnayn as a righteous world-conqueror granted divine pathways across the earth, explaining 'setting in a muddy spring' as either how the western ocean appeared to his eye or the sun's literal western station.
discussion.reply: In the early seventh-century Syriac Christian Legend Concerning Alexander, Alexander prays to God as the king upon whose head God placed two horns to thrust down the kingdoms of the world, marches to the fetid western sea where the sun enters the window of heaven, and travels east to the people who have no shelter from the rising sun's heat.

cards.quranEn: [83] They ask you about Dhū-l-Qarnayn. Say: ‘I shall recite to you a remembrance of him. [84] Surely We established him on the earth and gave him a way of access to everything. [85] He followed (one such) way of access [86] until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and he found next to it a people. We said, “Dhū-l-Qarnayn! Either punish (them) or do them (some) good.” [87] He said, “As for the one who does evil, we shall punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him (with) a terrible punishment. [88] But as for the one who believes, and does righteousness, for him (there is) the good payment, and we shall speak to him something easy from our command.” [89] Then he followed (another) way of access [90] until, when he reached the rising (place) of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not provided any shelter from it. [91] So (it was), but We had already encompassed what his situation was in (our) awareness.

cards.title: Solomon Reviewing the Birds, the Missing Hoopoe, and News from Sheba
cards.note: Surah 27:20–28 narrates Solomon inspecting his birds, threatening the absent hoopoe (hudhud), hearing its report on the sun-worshipping Queen of Sheba, and dispatching a letter by bird, reproducing Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Solomon employed the hoopoe as a scout to locate underground water during his military marches and sent it with a royal letter summoning Bilqis, the Queen of Sheba, to submit to God.
discussion.reply: In 1 Kings 10:1–2, the Queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's fame and travels to Jerusalem without any bird messenger. In the Galilean Aramaic Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2, Solomon misses the wild cock (hoopoe) during a feast, threatens to destroy it in anger, hears its report of a wealthy eastern city ruled by the Queen of Sheba, and binds a letter to its wing.

cards.quranEn: [20] He reviewed the birds, and said, ‘Why do I not see the hudhud? Or is it one of the absent? [21] I shall indeed punish it severely, or slaughter it, or it will bring me a clear authority.’ [22] But it did not stay (away) for long, and said, ‘I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have brought you reliable news from (the people of) Sheba. [23] Surely I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given (some) of everything, and she has a great throne. [24] I found her and her people prostrating themselves before the sun instead of God. Satan has made their deeds appear enticing to them, and he has kept them from the way, and they are not (rightly) guided. [25] (He did this) so that they would not prostrate themselves before God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. He knows what you hide and what you speak aloud. [26] God – (there is) no god but Him, Lord of the great throne.’ [27] He said, ‘We shall see whether you have spoken the truth or are one of the liars. [28] Go with this letter of mine, and cast it (down) to them. Then turn away from them and see what they return.’
quranHighlights: He reviewed the birds, and said, ‘Why do I not see the hudhud?
I have brought you reliable news from (the people of) Sheba. [23] Surely I found a woman ruling over them
and she has been given (some) of everything
Go with this letter of mine, and cast it (down) to them.

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.ref: Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 (Report on Sheba)
sources.en: I looked and saw a country in the land of the East; Kitor is the name of its city. Its dust is more precious than gold, and silver lies like dung in its streets. Trees have stood planted there since the beginning of the world, and they drink water from the Garden of Eden. Great multitudes live there with crowns on their heads, planted there from the Garden of Eden. They do not know how to fight in battle, and they cannot shoot with the bow. But truly I saw one woman who rules over all of them, and her name is the Queen of Sheba.

Its dust is more precious than gold, and silver lies like dung in its streets
But truly I saw one woman who rules over all of them, and her name is the Queen of Sheba.

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.ref: Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 (Letter Tied to Wing)
sources.en: The king’s scribes were summoned, and they wrote a letter and tied the letter to the wing of the wild rooster. It rose and went up into the heights of the sky, whirled aloft, gathered its strength and flew among the birds, and they flew after it, and they went to the city of Kitor, to the land of Sheba. In the morning the Queen of Sheba went out to worship the sea, and the birds darkened the sun. She took hold of her clothes and tore them, and she was utterly astonished. While she was utterly astonished, the wild rooster came down to her, and she saw that a letter was tied to its wing.

cards.title: Pharaoh Commanding Haman to Build a Tower to the Ropes of the Heavens
cards.note: In Surah 40:36–37, Pharaoh orders Haman to build a tower (sarhan) to reach the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat) and look upon Moses' God, merging Genesis 11:3–4 (Babel), Esther 3:1 (Haman), and the aerial castle of the Story of Ahikar.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Pharaoh commanded his vizier Haman to construct a high brick tower in Egypt so Pharaoh could ascend toward the pathways of the sky and test Moses' claim regarding the God of heaven.
discussion.reply: Unlike 28:38, which specifies baking clay bricks, 40:36–37 focuses on reaching the 'ropes of the heavens' (asbab al-samawat). The passage merges three ancient traditions separated by centuries: the Tower of Babel built to reach heaven in Genesis 11:3–4, the Persian court minister Haman under King Artaxerxes in Esther 3:1, and Pharaoh's demand for a castle between heaven and earth in the Story of Ahikar.

cards.quranEn: [36] Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes, [37] the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses. Surely I think he is a liar indeed.’ In this way the evil of his deed was made to appear enticing to Pharaoh, and he was kept from the way. But the plot of Pharaoh only (came) to ruin.
quranHighlights: Pharaoh said, ‘Haman! Build a tower for me, so that I may reach the ropes,
the ropes of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses.

cards.title: Surah 2 Covenant Reminder of Mount Sinai Raised Above Israel
cards.note: Surah 2:63 addresses the Children of Israel directly, recalling how God took their covenant while raising the mountain physically above them (rafa'na fawqakumu l-tura), reproducing the midrashic reading of Exodus 19:17 in Talmud Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report from Ibn 'Abbas that when the Israelites hesitated to accept the heavy obligations of the Torah, angels uprooted Mount Sinai and held it suspended over their heads until they bowed in acceptance.
discussion.reply: While 7:171 uses nataqna ('We shook the mountain above them as a canopy'), 2:63 states the motif in the second person (rafa'na fawqakumu l-tura) during Israel's covenant indictment. In Exodus 19:17 the Israelites stand at the foot (be-tachtit) of Mount Sinai; Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a and Avodah Zarah 2b read be-tachtit literally ('beneath') to teach that God overturned the mountain above them like a tub.

cards.quranEn: (Remember) when We took a covenant with you, and raised the mountain above you: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and remember what is in it, so that you may guard (yourselves).’

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 88a
sources.en: Rabbi Avdimi bar Ḥama bar Ḥasa said: the Jewish people actually stood beneath the mountain, and the verse teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, overturned the mountain above the Jews like a tub, and said to them: If you accept the Torah, excellent, and if not, there will be your burial.
